newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, China sign joint political declaration.
newsitem.headline: Russia, China sign joint political declaration.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Chinese President Jiang Zemin signed on Wednesday a political declaration outlining their joint vision of the post-Cold War world, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The text of the declaration was not immediately available but Russian officials have said the document includes a clause in which Beijing and Moscow would express their opposition to "claims by any country to the role of absolute leader."
Interfax news agency quoted Yeltsin as saying that the document was unprecedented in Russia's relations with other countries.

"Someone is longing for a single-polar world," Interfax quoted Yeltsin as saying after the signing ceremony. "But we want the world to be multi-polar. Those poles will form the basis of the new international order."

Yeltsin did not mention any country but his remark clearly referred to the claims by the United States for the leading role in the post-Cold War world which aroused jealousy both in Moscow and Beijing.

Officials from both countries have said that the declaration was the key bilateral document to be signed during Jiang's five-day state visit to Moscow. Russia, China, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan are also to sign a treaty on troop reductions along the former Soviet-Chinese border.
